text:
Maria: Bringing up hartley-3b on dev-staging — quick checklist + sanity prompts. pinging @Aj @Liam @Sophia for prioritization.

Maria: Quick checklist: 1) short generation smoke, 2) instruction-following, 3) embeddings similarity, 4) basic arithmetic & dates, 5) perf p50/p95.

Aj: Can you drop the sample prompts so I can run the smoke harness?

Maria: sample prompts:
```
1) "Write a 3-line summary of why caching helps LLM inference."
2) "Solve: 17 * 24 = ?"
3) "Translate to French: 'Our meeting is on Thursday.'"
```

Liam: quick heads-up — after int8 quant we saw wrong multiplication results on the arithmetic prompt (17*24 -> 428). Suspect activation clipping/scale issue. Repro snippet:
```
python eval.py --model hartley-3b-int8 --prompt "17 * 24 = ?" --n 20
# observed 428 in 7/20 samples
```

Sophia: is this only on int8? float16 still ok?

Liam: float16 passes. int8 has ~1.6x throughput improvement but shows regressions on math and some date formats.

Evan: I can run a targeted 1k-sample eval (math + dates + tokenization anchors) tonight and upload metrics to the evals bucket.

Maria: please log results under /evals/devstg/hartley-3b and include seed + tokenizer version. If regression confirmed we should: 1) revert quant profile for critical endpoints, 2) add failing prompts to regression suite, 3) test alternate quant algorithms (GPTQ vs AWQ) and different clipping strategies.

deploy-bot: Deploy successful: hartley-3b-int8 -> dev-staging (instances: 4), started 1868123470

Maria: noted. Prioritization: smoke-only -> low, arithmetic/date regressions -> high (affects downstream products). @Aj @Liam please align on whether to pause int8 rollout.

Aj: I recommend HOLD for production. I'll update the rollout ticket and tag infra.

Liam: I'll start a binary-search over quant bits and run a tuned 200-prompt sweep to isolate failure modes.

Sophia: add a note to include LLM-qa and date/format tests into nightly evals so this doesn't slip through.

Maria: thanks — I'll open a reproducible-steps issue, attach logs and samples, and mark P1 for triage. :thumbsup:
